summary: Piscataquis County, ME lookout site from 1913; 1915 station, 1920 records conflict on tower versus cabin, staffed in 1953; FFLA lists it standing, cab gone.

facts.design: Wood station with three-foot peeled spruce underpinning (1915 report); later structure type not described in sources read
facts.status_note: FFLA marks it Standing* (cab no longer in place); date and cause of cab removal not found

events.note: New station erected with three-foot peeled spruce underpinning and wired down (1916 Forest Commissioner's report, as quoted)
Inventory calls the station a wood ground cabin; a 1920 Maine State Archives panoramic map is centered on the Beetle Mt. fire tower. Sources disagree.
Robert Blackmore served as lookout for the State Forest Fire Warden Service on Beetle Mountain

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The 1920 inventory calls the station a wood ground cabin, while the 1920 Maine State Archives map calls it the Beetle Mt. fire tower. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: The brief record calls it a tower and gives no height or design; the 1915 and 1920 sources describe a station and a ground cabin, so 'tower' rests on the FFLA listing and the 1920 map title. A 2021 firelookout.org inventory appeared only in a search snippet (reportedly: tower without cab, groundhouse in bad condition, and a steel tower from 1965); its URL could not be fetched, so it is not used. Verify before adding any 1965 steel-tower event. The 1953 Blackmore item is a bear anecdote reprinted from the Biddeford Journal; only the lookout attribution is used.
